title: Common questions about what you need for your driving test
summary: This page provides common questions and requirements for taking a practical driving test in NSW.
who_can_apply: Older drivers or if you have a medical condition
what_you_need: A registered, safe, and roadworthy vehicle that matches the licence type you are applying for.
Proof of identity, including your learner, overseas, or full driver licence.
The completed licence application form (available online or at the service centre).
Payment or concession card for the licence fee (some service centres only accept card payments).
Glasses or contact lenses for the eyesight test.

faqs.q: What do I need to bring for my driving test?
faqs.a: You need to bring proof of identity, such as your learner, overseas, or full driver licence. It is also recommended to bring your payment or concession card for the licence fee, as some service centres only accept card payments.

faqs.q: What should I do before my driving test?
faqs.a: You should check that your vehicle is registered, safe, roadworthy, and appropriate for the licence you want. You must also arrive at least 15 minutes before your test time and park in the designated Driving Test parking bays.

faqs.q: Do I need to prepare for the eyesight test?
faqs.a: Yes, you may need to pass an eyesight test, so bring your glasses or wear contact lenses.
